## ✨ Highlights

- 🔒 **A security update for every node**: IPv6 is now hardened from the first second of a boot - a host on a node's network can no longer steer its IPv6 traffic with a router advertisement sent while it boots (🟡 medium).
- 💡 **Kernel values suggested for each node**: the node watches its own saturation signals, hour by hour, and suggests values for the kernel parameters HAProxy depends on - each with its rule, its measurements and its sources. Never applied by itself: you test it on trial, like any change.
- 🛡️ **keepalived confined further**: the VRRP extension's daemon can no longer change any kernel parameter.

## 🔒 Security

For **every node**:

- 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-003](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.10.07-2/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-003.json) - **a host on a node's network could steer its IPv6 traffic** with ICMPv6 redirects and router advertisements: read or alter what TLS doesn't protect - HAProxy's plain-HTTP connections to servers, for instance - or drop it. Before v2026.10.07 a node accepted both on every interface; v2026.10.07 refused them once the node was up, but the interface the kernel brings up for DHCP, before Janus's init, could still take an advertisement in the first seconds of a boot - and keep its address and default route. Now IPv6 starts off, in the signed kernel command line, and init turns it on only once every interface refuses redirects and advertisements.

  It concerns you if a host that shouldn't steer your nodes' traffic can reach their network - another machine on a shared VLAN, for instance.

**Besides updating**: nothing - the reboot that ends the update drops any address or route an advertisement gave.

## 💡 Suggested kernel values

- **What the node observes**: every 15 seconds, the kernel's own counters and gauges - accept queue overflows, SYN cookies, TCP memory pressure, dropped packets, open files, the connection tracking table - and, every minute, the source ports in use towards each server and the rate of outgoing connections. By hour, kept 14 days. **System › Sysctl › What the node observed** shows each signal - as does `janusctl system sysctl observed`.
- **When it suggests**: a signal counts once seen in 3 different hours of the last 7 days - a saturation that comes back, never one peak. Then the rules, each written out with its sources: `net.core.somaxconn` doubled when accept queues overflow at it, the widest source port range when one server takes half the ports, `tcp_tw_reuse` above 300 connections a second, `tcp_synack_retries` 2 under SYN cookies, the input backlog doubled on drops, open files and the conntrack table twice their peak, smaller TCP buffers under memory pressure - and, from the node's memory, a `somaxconn` that keeps full queues to an eighth of it (16384 on 1 GiB with one listener) and a conntrack table sized for a load balancer when connections are tracked. See [the rules](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/kernel-tuning.md#the-rules).
- **Never applied by itself**: on the page, **Why** shows the rule, what it measured and its sources, **Use** puts the value in the table - then you test it on trial and apply it. A suggestion stays within the parameter's bounds and passes the same checks as a change: one the node would refuse isn't shown.
- **janusctl**: `system sysctl list` gets a SUGGESTED column, `system sysctl get NAME` the suggestion in full, with the command that tests it.

## 🛡️ Hardening

- **keepalived reads kernel parameters, never writes them** (SELinux): only Janus's init writes the CIS benchmark's keys, and no daemon can write `kernel.core_pattern`.
- **VRRP**: the check now refuses `use_vmac`, `use_ipvlan` and `disable_local_igmp` with the reason - Janus's kernel has neither macvlan nor ipvlan interfaces (they could never work), and a VMAC needs `net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter` at 0, which the CIS benchmark forbids. See [VRRP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/vrrp.md#a-configuration).
- **Raspberry Pi images**: Yama in their kernel - the CIS benchmark's 33 kernel-parameter controls hold there too.

## 🔌 The node API

- `SystemService.SysctlList`: a parameter's `recommendation` is now filled - its value, rule, measurements and sources - and the response's new `observation` gives the signals the node observed, by hour. Nothing else changed.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Controller first**, as usual: it shows the suggestions of the nodes on this release.
- **IPv6 starts once the node is hardened**: nothing to do - static IPv6 configurations come up as before.
- **A keepalived.conf with `use_vmac`, `use_ipvlan` or `disable_local_igmp`** is refused when applied - one already saved keeps running as it did.
